title: PRIMO Dictionary-Learning ML Sharpens the First M87* Supermassive Black Hole Image to Nominal EHT Resolution
whyItMatters: Published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, PRIMO trained on 30,000 GRMHD black-hole simulations to fill sparse Event Horizon Telescope interferometry gaps, halving the ring width of M87* to the telescope’s full diffraction limit.
summary: Published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters on April 13, 2023, Lia Medeiros (IAS), Dimitrios Psaltis, Tod R. Lauer (NOIRLab), and Feryal Özel introduced PRIMO (Principal-component Interferometric Modeling), a dictionary-learning machine learning algorithm trained on over 30,000 high-fidelity general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations of accreting black holes. Applied to the original 2017 Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) observations of M87*, PRIMO reconstructed missing Earth-sized interferometer baselines without inventing unsupported structure—producing an image consistent with EHT data that narrowed the bright emission ring by roughly a factor of two and sharpened constraints on M87*’s mass and general relativity.
technicalHighlights: Trained principal-component dictionary learning on >30,000 simulated black hole images spanning diverse accretion physics.
Reconstructed missing sparse VLBI Fourier-plane data to reach the Event Horizon Telescope’s full nominal angular resolution.
Revealed a ring roughly twice as thin as the 2019 reconstruction with a deeper central shadow, improving black-hole mass precision.
caveats: Image reconstruction depends on the GRMHD simulation training prior (assuming general-relativistic accretion physics); it refines observational inference from existing 2017 EHT data rather than discovering a new astrophysical object.

scoreRationale.foundational: Pioneered simulation-trained machine-learning interferometric reconstruction at the physical diffraction limit of an Earth-scale radio telescope.
scoreRationale.ripple: Became an iconic demonstration of physics-informed ML in observational astrophysics and next-generation EHT / Sagittarius A* imaging.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in The Astrophysical Journal Letters (947:L7) with extensive synthetic-data fidelity and consistency checks against EHT visibilities.
scoreRationale.velocity: Extracted full-resolution physical structure from existing sparse observations years ahead of launching space-based VLBI antennas.
